_comment: Second half — run against the SAME session key right after episode-multiturn-initial's turn:1 completes. turn:1 is done (not parked), so the starter mints a fresh turn:2. This message answers the agent's clarifying question, so ClassifyRequest should return continues_prior=true and OpenEpisode should ATTACH turn:2 to turn:1's still-open episode — no new episode, no new plan seed, no re-routing (memory + tools run per-turn now). episode-multiturn-followup.expect.sh checks both turns share one episode_id and that exactly one skill_candidates row is written for the whole two-turn trajectory (after the ~30s idle close).

message.content: Global across the service, and assume 10k RPS at peak. Walk me through the approach.

scripted_model_responses.content: Got it — global, 10k RPS. Checking what rate-limiting primitives we already have available.

arguments.query: existing rate limiting middleware redis token bucket

scripted_model_responses.content: Approach: a token-bucket limiter backed by Redis, one global bucket refilled at 10k tokens/sec with a burst ceiling of ~15k. Each edge node does an atomic DECR against the shared counter via a Lua script so the check-and-decrement is race-free; if Redis is unreachable the limiter fails open. That keeps the hot path to a single round-trip and the limit genuinely global rather than per-node.
